rawItems.title: Blaze no longer a major incident as firefighters thanked for 'unwavering' effort
rawItems.content: The fire at a Cambridgeshire nature reserve is no longer being treated as a major incident. Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service said today that national resilience crews have been stood down after supporting the response to the blaze at Holme Fen for the past fortnight. Firefighters will remain at the nature reserve while clearance work continues and crews monitor for hotspots in the peat, which can continue burning underground. The service is reducing its presence to two crews during the day and one overnight, with the level of response to be reviewed daily. The national resilience crews were stood down at Holme Fen, marking a significant milestone in the incident. Chief Fire Officer Matthew Warren and Deputy Chief Fire Officer Jon Anderson met the firefighters at lunchtime to thank them personally for all their hard work in supporting our response. (Image: Cambs Fire and Rescue) Chief Fire Officer Matthew Warren and Deputy Chief Fire Officer Jon Anderson met firefighters at the scene at lunchtime today (Monday) to personally thank them for their work. Mr Warren said the support from firefighters drafted in from other services across the country had been essential, both in tackling the fire and in keeping Cambridgeshire crews available for other emergencies.
